status_summary: On 2025-10-16 S. 3014, the Ensuring Timely Access to Generics Act of 2025, was introduced and referred to the Senate HELP Committee; per the committee's section-by-section summary it would let FDA deny citizen petitions filed mainly to delay a generic or biosimilar, and it does not address samples or 180-day exclusivity. The bill status record shows no action on S. 3014 after referral; a 2026-06-17 HELP markup that included it was reported by Bloomberg Government as delaying the vote on it. A citizen-petition provision of the same title was carried in the INSULIN Act of 2026 (S. 4189), which the committee ordered reported on 2026-07-22 and reported on 2026-08-07 (Calendar No. 552). No FDA action directed at first-to-file exclusivity being held unused was found. Sample-access remedies for generics already exist in the 2019 CREATES Act, which predates the period.

timeline.event: S. 3014, the Ensuring Timely Access to Generics Act of 2025, was introduced by Senator Shaheen and referred to the Senate HELP Committee; the bill status record lists no later action.

The Senate HELP Committee held a markup that included S. 3014; after a dispute over amendments the vote on the generics bill was delayed, per Bloomberg Government; the bill status record lists no committee action.

The Senate HELP Committee ordered the INSULIN Act of 2026 (S. 4189) reported with a substitute amendment; its reported text carries, as section 5, an 'Ensuring Timely Access to Generics' provision amending section 505(q) of the FD&C Act (a 180-day filing deadline for citizen petitions, factors for finding a petition was filed to delay approval, and dismissal of certain suits that skip the petition process). It does not address 180-day exclusivity or samples.
The HELP Committee reported S. 4189 to the Senate without a written report and it was placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar (Calendar No. 552).

title: Stop unused first-generic exclusivity; generic sample access; bar meritless petitions
uncertainties: The introduction date, sponsor and referral were confirmed in the BILLSTATUS XML for S. 3014, which lists nothing after referral. The 2026-06-17 markup delay rests on one Bloomberg Government report, opened in part in review (the dispute over amendments and the delayed vote are visible); a law-firm alert (Akin Gump) says the committee approved S. 3014 on 2026-06-17, which conflicts with the report of a delay and with the empty bill status, so the markup outcome for S. 3014 is not established (the alert is not an official source). The reported S. 4189 text was read for the first 100,000 of 105,071 characters; its section 5 changes the petition filing deadline to 180 days after the information is known (the struck original text said 60 days), adds delay factors and requires dismissal of certain suits, so it differs from the S. 3014 summary in detail; its text on exclusivity and samples was not found in the part read. The House STOP GAMES Act (H.R. 8908, introduced 2026-05-19, referred to Energy and Commerce) covers similar ground; the alert reports a committee vote on 2026-07-21 that was not confirmed in the bill status record. A 2023 Senate press release shows an earlier version cleared the HELP Committee in the 118th Congress, before the period. The D.C. Circuit decision in Norwich v. Kennedy (August 2026, month-only) concerns FDA's forfeiture analysis for 180-day exclusivity and is not an FDA action to stop unused exclusivity. The Federal Register API returned no FDA documents on citizen petitions or 180-day exclusivity from 2025-01-20. Stage unchanged: a committee-reported vehicle for one of the three asks is still a bill pending in the Senate. In review the Akin Gump alert (dated 2026-08-07) was read: it lists S. 3014 as approved by HELP on 2026-06-17 and S. 4189 on 2026-07-22, and places the petition language in S. 4189 as section 301, whereas the reported text numbers it section 5; the official bill status records show no committee action on S. 3014 or H.R. 8908, so the alert's statements are not adopted.
